target_customer: Women who want to strengthen the pelvic floor, sold direct to consumer, including active women who exercise
problem: Pelvic floor weakness and leaking during exercise affect many women, and existing options require months of private regimens or clinical visits. Liv Labs offers a worn internal resistance spring that trains the pelvic floor during normal movement.
business_model: Direct to consumer hardware sales of the Pippa resistance spring kits, funded largely by non-dilutive grants
product_category: Women's health consumer device (pelvic floor fitness)

founders.name: Melody Roberts
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page. Described as a consumer convenience and service experience designer.

founders.name: Carly Price
founders.background_notes: YC page says she designed a reimagined pillow for Casper and holds 45 patents; employer not stated. Hypepotamus says she filed the provisional patent behind Pippa in 2017 and met Roberts in 1999.

competitors.name: Elvie
competitors.what: Smart pelvic floor trainer with app biofeedback, sold direct to consumers and through the NHS

technical_complexity.rationale: A medical grade silicone internal device needed patents, clinical evidence and SBIR funded development from 2017, but it is a passive spring with no electronics.

defensibility.rationale: The company cites a US patent and NIH SBIR backed clinical data and holds the PIPPA trademark filed in October 2021, but passive devices can be imitated.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying the exercise during activity wedge; the founders were still selling direct as of 2026.

market_need_then: The company cites 78 million US women with pelvic floor weakness and 31 million who worry daily about leaks. NIH, NSF and Illinois grants funded development, indicating federal interest in the problem.

branding.domain_note: Uses livlabsfitness.com rather than an exact liv labs domain; no purchase history found.

identity.visual_style: Consumer wellness storefront with accessories such as a canvas pouch and print bandana
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly and athletic, with labels such as PT recommended and Marathoner approved

branding.brand_signature: The Pippa product name and the sporty exercise positioning
branding.community_and_virality: A Kickstarter campaign earned a Project We Love badge; the company exhibited at the Atlanta Marathon expo in February 2026 and was a Fast Company 2025 Innovation by Design honoree per its own site.

brand_strength.rationale: Small direct to consumer brand with niche press and a Kickstarter badge; no evidence of wide recognition. The name Liv Labs is also shared by an unrelated MLM company, which is a minor confusion risk.

outcome_analysis: Liv Labs stayed alive on mostly non-dilutive grants and a small team, reaching market with Pippa only around 2025 after years of development from the 2017 patent filing. It remains active in 2026 with direct sales and awards but no reported equity round or large traction figure, so the story is slow, capital efficient hardware development rather than venture scale growth.
notes: Funding: no equity round confirmed. NIH SEED showcase says over 2.6M raised; a search summary of a YC profile says 3.2M pre-seed with 80 percent SBIR grants (unverified); CB Insights 400K and VCBacked 563K are partial aggregator figures. A search summary also shows NIH award records of 722,496 (FY2022) and 563,008 (FY2024) that I did not open. None are recorded as rounds. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoff news. Competition search found no 2021 dated rivals beyond Elvie; Elidah and PeriCoach appear only in undated directories. Completeness pass: the University of Chicago Polsky Center (Aug 2021) says an NIH SBIR grant of up to 1.67M over two years (recorded as the ceiling, not confirmed paid) and over 200K from friends and family (recorded as 200K, a floor). Grant databases show NIH R44 awards of 951,491 (FY2021) and 722,496 (FY2022), which overlap the 1.67M and are not recorded separately. An NSF award of 255,078 is listed in a search summary (date not seen) and not recorded. Round dates are the article year.
